boards.title: Your First Weekend at Randolph-Macon College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A campus-centered, under-21-safe first-weekend sequence: get oriented, share a meal, explore academic and creative spaces, then join recurring student programming.

cards.title: Start at Brock Commons
cards.subtitle: Student Engagement Center • 304 Henry Street
cards.notes: Stop by the Student Engagement Center to ask about clubs, service, outdoor leadership, esports, and weekend programming before choosing your next stop.
cards.short_summary: Use the student-life hub to turn a free afternoon into a concrete plan.
cards.evidence_claim: RMC identifies the Student Engagement Center in Brock Commons as headquarters for clubs and activities, including leadership, service, and late-night programming.
cards.access_notes: Student Engagement Center is on the second floor; ask staff about current events and participation requirements.

cards.title: Make a meal-plan stop at Estes
cards.subtitle: 306 Henry Street
cards.notes: Meet a new classmate for a meal, then use the spacious servery layout as an easy place to compare weekend plans and campus tips.
cards.short_summary: A practical shared-meal stop in RMC’s renovated dining hall.
cards.evidence_claim: RMC completed Estes Dining Hall renovations for 2024–2025, including a renovated serving area, expanded seating, and multiple food stations.
cards.source_title: Renovated Estes Dining Hall Opens for 2024-2025 | Randolph-Macon College
cards.access_notes: Bring your RMC ID; College policy states IDs are used to eat at Estes Dining Hall.

cards.title: Get your bearings at the fountain
cards.subtitle: Brown Fountain Plaza • 300 Henry Street
cards.notes: Use the fountain plaza as a meeting point, take a campus photo, and notice the surrounding residence halls before heading to your next activity.
cards.short_summary: A recognizable central plaza for an unhurried campus reset.
cards.evidence_claim: RMC’s virtual tour describes Frank E. Brown Fountain Plaza as a central student meeting place for relaxing, studying, and events.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor plaza; use it as a meeting point and follow any event setup or campus-use guidance.

cards.title: Find a study base at McGraw-Page
cards.subtitle: McGraw-Page Library
cards.notes: Tour the first floor, ask a librarian about support, and bookmark the Abernathy Room if you need a dependable late study space later.
cards.short_summary: A research, collaboration, and 24/7 student-study stop.
cards.evidence_claim: The library provides research, study, and collaboration spaces; its Abernathy Room is a 24/7 study space, and services are free to students.
cards.source_title: McGraw-Page Library | Randolph-Macon College Academic Catalog
cards.access_notes: The Abernathy Room is identified as 24/7 student study space; RMC IDs are used to check out library books.

cards.title: Check the arts venues
cards.subtitle: Center for the Performing Arts • 205 Henry Street
cards.notes: Walk by the performing-arts complex and look for a public concert or theatre listing that fits your weekend; confirm entry details before attending.
cards.short_summary: A campus arts stop linking music, theatre, rehearsal, and performance spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: RMC’s Center for the Performing Arts houses the music and theatre programs and connects to Blackwell Auditorium.
cards.access_notes: Attendance and ticket requirements vary by performance; consult the specific event listing.

cards.title: Move at the Brock Center
cards.subtitle: 313 N. Center Street
cards.notes: Bring your RMC ID, take a quick facility orientation, and choose a low-key activity such as the indoor track, courts, or lap swimming if available.
cards.short_summary: A campus recreation stop with courts, a track, pool, and climbing wall.
cards.evidence_claim: The Brock Center includes an aquatics center, indoor running track, multi-purpose courts, fitness facilities, and an 18-foot climbing wall.
cards.source_title: Brock Sports and Recreation Center | Randolph-Macon College
cards.access_notes: Entry requires a valid RMC ID or director’s pass; verify posted operating hours before going.

cards.title: Look for an outdoor adventure
cards.subtitle: Weekend activities organized through RMC
cards.notes: Check The BUZZ for an upcoming outdoor-leadership trip, then sign up only after reviewing the specific activity, transportation, equipment, and participation details.
cards.short_summary: A structured route to explore Virginia outdoors with other RMC students.
cards.evidence_claim: RMC reports that Outdoor Leadership offers weekend adventures during the semester, including hiking, rock climbing, apple picking, horseback riding, and rafting.
cards.source_title: Learning Beyond the Classroom: Getting Involved at RMC | Randolph-Macon College
cards.access_notes: Trips and eligibility vary; check The BUZZ and the specific trip information before registering.

cards.title: Meet organizations at Activities Carnival
cards.subtitle: Annual involvement event at Fountain Plaza
cards.notes: When the carnival is scheduled, circle the tables that genuinely interest you, ask how beginners join, and save one contact for a follow-up meeting.
cards.short_summary: An annual campus event for connecting directly with student organizations.
cards.evidence_claim: RMC describes Activities Carnival as its premier annual involvement event, with dozens of student-organization tables around Fountain Plaza.
cards.source_title: Learning Beyond the Classroom: Getting Involved at RMC | Randolph-Macon College
cards.access_notes: Annual event; confirm date and participating organizations through current RMC event channels.

cards.title: Choose a Friday After Five event
cards.subtitle: Friday nights during fall and spring terms
cards.notes: Check the current listing after 5 p.m., pick one campus program that interests you, and use it as a low-pressure way to meet people.
cards.short_summary: Recurring free Friday-night programming organized by RMC groups.
cards.evidence_claim: RMC describes Fridays After Five as free student events on Friday nights after 5 p.m. during fall and spring semesters.
cards.access_notes: Offered during fall and spring terms; the page currently shows no upcoming events, so confirm the semester calendar first.

cards.title: Close Saturday at Late Night Brock
cards.subtitle: Brock Commons • Saturday, 10 p.m.–midnight
cards.notes: If classes are in session, check the current program first, then bring a friend to the Saturday-night social activity at Brock Commons.
cards.short_summary: Recurring, free student programming that runs late on Saturday nights.
cards.evidence_claim: RMC states that Late Night Brock provides free student programming at Brock Commons on Saturday nights during fall and spring semesters.
cards.access_notes: Direct current-hours evidence: held Saturdays from 10:00 p.m. to midnight during fall and spring semesters; confirm the current schedule before attending.

warnings: Weekend programs are term-dependent; confirm the current RMC event calendar and access requirements before going.
